paragraphs.text: Bill and Michelle Martin and Nick Chan.
Can we show them the stable and the horses?
Happy to meet you, said Uncle George.
He was a big man of about 40 with long black hair, a silver necklace, and friendly dark eyes.
Come with me and we'll visit this stable.
The sheriff and his men are here too.
They are looking at the horses.
They entered the big stable and saw a sign on the wall.
Riding lessons on Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday at 10 a.m. and 4 p.m.
Some people were cleaning the horses and the stable, and others were getting ready to ride.
Uncle George laughed and gave Nick Bill and Michelle some sugar cubes.
Here, you can give them to the horses.
It's a good way to make friends with a horse.
I want to show you Ginger, a beautiful Arabian stallion, and my favorite horse.
When they left the stable, they saw the sheriff and Professor Massey talking with Uncle George.
We'll come back later today, said Sheriff Lopez.
Professor Massey wants to check something at the university.
The sheriff got into his car and drove away.
Professor Massey smiled at Uncle George and said, don't worry George.
We're just checking a few things.
You know me and my people.
Wild Wolf said a lot of strange things and he didn't like Richardson.
Today the sheriff's going to talk to Luke Langley.
Langley hated Richardson, and everyone knows that.
He never even talked to him.
No one wants to buy Langley's houses.
He had a good reason to kill Richardson.
Uncle George and Massey talked for a few minutes.
And then Massey got into his jeep and drove away.
Oh, that cool jeep belongs to the Professor.
And he has a personalized plate too.
After lunch, Pam took her friends to visit the Chumash Museum.
Before leaving the reservation, they went back to the stable.
Look, the sheriff's back again, said Bill.
And he's talking to my uncle.
We think the horse of the Richardson murder comes from your stable.
We found some war paint on several horses.
We put war paint on the horses yesterday morning before the parade.
And yesterday evening we washed most of it off.
Do you lock the stable doors at night?
But it's not difficult to get into the stables.
We always keep a few windows open for the horses because they need fresh air.
Anyone can get in through an open window.
Where were you last night at about eleven o'clock?
I suspect all of the men on this reservation.
I was here at the reservation with my father.
Did you see or hear anything unusual at the stable?
The stable is far from my house and the other houses.
Sheriff, can I ask you a question?
Did you find any fingerprints on the spear?
But the spear is a Chumash spear.
There are many of them at the Chumash Museum.
Did you talk to Luke Langley?
He was driving to a party in Hollywood last night.
But no one was with him.
The sheriff walked back to his car and got in.
Suddenly, his cell phone rang and he answered it.
I just talked to the Los Angeles police.
They said Luke Langley has just driven across the Mexican border.
I gave the border police his name early this afternoon.
He's left the United States so it's going to be hard to find him now.
I've got to contact the Mexican police.
The sheriff's car drove off quickly.
Said Pam, going to her uncle.
The sheriff suspects all of the men on the reservation.
We were sitting on the bench near the stable.
No one on the reservation killed Jacob Richardson.
How can we discover the truth?
Suddenly, Wild Wolf came to the stable to talk to George.
Then, Wild Wolf looked at the four teenagers and smiled.
Perhaps there is a way to discover the truth.
There's a full moon tomorrow night.
George can pick you up at Portola Point and then he can drive you back.
